title: Restore Docker and VM metrics endpoint parity in the TUI
objective: PR #20 Phase 1 metrics regression (related to parent #35 and verification ticket #21): host-metrics-tui currently hardcodes the VM metrics address, while the Docker agent uses the Compose service name. Compare with feat/vm-approach and restore working Docker and VM behavior without weakening the VM egress/security architecture.

acceptance_criteria.text: The shared host-metrics TUI selects a reachable metrics endpoint correctly in Docker-agent and direct-in-VM modes without relying on inaccessible addresses.
Automated regression tests cover endpoint selection and metrics fetching behavior for both Docker and VM modes, including missing/invalid configuration handling.
VM mode continues to use the approved metrics route and does not add host ports, direct host/LAN access, or weaker egress restrictions.
Existing metrics UI behavior and rendering remain intact; Docker and VM verification commands pass where the environment allows.

needed: Compare current plugin and agent startup/configuration with feat/vm-approach baseline.
Add regression tests for Docker and VM endpoint selection plus fetch failure handling.
Run unit/build checks for both modes; run Docker/VM runtime smoke only on authorized available environment.

Run Docker Compose metrics/TUI smoke and actual VM guest metrics/TUI smoke in authorized capable environment; this container has no Docker daemon or /dev/kvm. Verify both history and metrics display live data and sidebar remains healthy.
Sol independent review of the focused metrics implementation before its separate commit.
Sol re-review after prototype-key fix and CI wiring.
Owner/authorized environment runs Docker Compose and direct-VM live metrics/TUI smoke; verify live /metrics and /history fetches and healthy compact/expanded sidebar rendering.

Investigate CI-44935595188 same-disk restart: reproduce actual LoopbackServer immediate shutdown/rebind on an isolated loopback port without KVM; prove legitimate immediate restart works while a competing active listener is rejected; preserve fixed production 127.0.0.1:32129 endpoint and no sleeps/random ports/process killing. Inspect systemd ordering and feat/vm-approach history, distinguishing facts from hypotheses. Repair same-disk persistence evidence so its marker is stored on guest-disk-backed state, not virtiofs /workspace, and assert mount/filesystem placement.

Persistence marker path safety refinement: do not mkdir -p through guest-controlled components before lstat/open checks. Prefer a unique marker directly in the already provisioned private /home/mester/.local/state (guest UID 1000, mode 0700); open/traverse with dirfd + O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, create the marker with O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW, and validate the state directory device/filesystem equals guest root and is not virtiofs before writing and after restart. Preserve marker on failure and remove only after verified content. Add regression for symlinked state path refusal without writes.

Final Sol-approved persistence fixture design: use a unique marker directly in pre-provisioned /home/mester/.local/state; traverse /→home→mester→.local→state using dirfds and O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, verify owner/mode, and create/open/unlink only relative to the verified state dir fd with O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW. Verify root MAJ:MIN resolves through sysfs to the virtio_blk whole disk, and marker mount ID/device equals guest root and is not virtiofs, both before writing and after same-disk reboot. Preserve the marker on every failure. Regression-test symlink refusal at each path component without outside creation; valid partition-to-virtio_blk topology; and fail-closed overlay/virtiofs/unrelated/missing topology.
created: agent/opencode/plugins/host-metrics-tui/metrics-endpoint.js (+ declaration): fixed mode allowlist maps docker→http://metrics:19532 and vm→http://10.0.2.100:19532; only /metrics and /history?n=60 allowed; rejects missing/unknown mode, arbitrary endpoint/path, non-2xx and network errors.

tests/host-metrics-tui.test.mjs: Node mock-fetch tests both endpoints/resources and missing/invalid config; includes constructor, __proto__, and toString mode names to ensure inherited object properties fail closed. Added to .github/workflows/ci.yml VM unit/contract job.
tests/vm-parent-qemu.test.py: launch-boundary regression checks Compose Docker mode/internal metrics service/no ports and VM mode/existing guestfwd/restrict=on.

VM asset propagation updated and covered: lab-vm dependency bundle, system installer and update allowlist, owner acceptance install archive, protected cloud-init asset/digest, system acceptance byte comparison, hosted installer fixture.
cases: Sol review of focused BindPaths commit 75dbd59 identified Docker regression: TUI plugin hardcodes 10.0.2.100:19532 while Docker metrics service is metrics:19532; metrics is Phase 1 acceptance, not optional.

Delegated comparison with current HEAD and feat/vm-approach (97af1d83): shared TUI endpoint selector using METRICS_URL with Compose DNS default existed before fd87d22; fd87d22 hardcoded the VM guestfwd address for both TUI fetches. Current Docker agent lacks METRICS_URL and can resolve metrics:19532 only on the internal Compose network. Direct VM endpoint is 10.0.2.100:19532 via existing QEMU guestfwd to loopback metrics listener; retain restrict=on and no host ports.

Delegated security review: inject a fixed, trusted mode-specific endpoint at the launch boundary (Compose Docker agent and protected direct-VM launcher); do not accept workspace-controlled arbitrary URLs. Test both history and metrics fetch paths, malformed/missing config, errors, and assert network invariants (internal Compose service, exact guestfwd/restrict=on, no new host forwarding). No Docker/VM operations were run.

Sol pre-implementation design review (2026-11-21): APPROVE conditionally for `allow_reuse_address=True` on the actual fixed-loopback ThreadingHTTPServer, only with immediate same-port rebind and active-listener EADDRINUSE regressions, then hosted confirmation. Delegated actual-server reproduction (isolated 127.0.0.1:59077; production endpoint untouched): GET /metrics returned 200; competing second active server failed errno 98 while first remained responsive; after shutdown/close/join no LISTEN remained but /proc/net/tcp showed state 06 TIME_WAIT and immediate rebind failed errno 98. This establishes the local TIME_WAIT mechanism, not yet the hosted production fix. Acceptance marker currently resides in virtiofs `/workspace`; design approved to move it to verified guest-disk-backed state, preserve on failure, and remove only after successful same-disk proof. No KVM/production VM operation.

Design refinement pending Sol: initial implementation used mkdir -p for an unprovisioned /home/mester/.local/state/little-mester/acceptance before lstat checks. Delegated inspection found the guest provisioning helper safely prepares /home/mester/.local/state as mester-owned mode 0700, but exposes no API for the nested path; mkdir -p could follow a pre-existing symlink and create outside the intended directory. Do not continue that implementation until Sol reviews the simpler direct-state-directory + descriptor-relative no-follow creation approach. No hosted/VM operation.

Sol design refinement verdict: FIX on nested mkdir-p path due symlink traversal; delegated inspection confirmed prepared private /home/mester/.local/state but no safe nested-dir API. Follow-up design was revised to use that existing directory directly and walk every path component from / with dirfds/O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, checking ownership/mode/mount. Verify guest root MAJ:MIN via sysfs ancestry to virtio_blk (do not assume /dev/vda name), marker mount ID/device matches root, and use dirfd-relative O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW marker create/remove. Sol APPROVED this revised design provided verified dirfds are used throughout and all checks fail closed. Implementation/tests not yet revised; no VM/host operation.

CI-44935595188 metrics/persistence follow-up local implementation (not hosted acceptance): fixed loopback ThreadingHTTPServer now allows address reuse; actual-server regressions prove immediate same-port rebind after shutdown and reject a competing active listener (errno EADDRINUSE), preserving active listener. Persistence acceptance now writes unique marker directly in pre-provisioned /home/mester/.local/state, traverses each component with O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW dirfds, validates private owner/modes, same mount ID/device as guest root, and root block sysfs ancestry to virtio_blk (no /dev/vda assumption); marker create/verify/unlink are dirfd-relative and failure preserves marker. vm-systemd tests execute the embedded guest helper against a temporary root/sysfs fixture, including valid partition→virtio_blk topology, symlink refusal at every path component without outside creation, and non-virtio_blk refusal.
